No IMD warning, just 3 hours to respond: Sivasagar DC on July 19 flash flood
Within one to two hours, the Dikhow, which originates in the Naga Hills, crossed its warning level, breached the danger mark & surged to its highest recorded flood level
File image of flood waters entering villages in Sivasagar. (Photo:@149_bn/X)
Sivasagar, Aug 1: Sivasagar district had barely three hours to react before unprecedented floodwaters from Nagaland’s hills overwhelmed rivers, cut off rescue teams and triggered one of the worst disasters in the district’s history on July 19, District Commissioner Mridul Yadav has revealed, describing the deluge as a “flash flood” that unfolded far too quickly for conventional disaster response.
According to Yadav, there was no warning from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) of extremely heavy rainfall that could have indicated the scale of the disaster. The administration first realised the gravity of the situation around 12:30 pm on July 19, when the Deputy Commissioner of Mokokchung in Nagaland called seeking boats for rescue operations, as several villages on the Nagaland side had already gone under water due to the rising level of the Jhanji River.
